question: Is Jefferson's Southwest Ridge distinct from our South Ridge (Pamelia Lake), or the same line?
answer: Distinct routes that merge high up. Both start at Pamelia Lake Trailhead, but the South Ridge leaves the PCT toward Mud Lake / Shale Lake and goes cross-country to the saddle between Goat Peak and Jefferson, then climbs the south ridge. The Southwest Ridge leaves the PCT about 20 minutes south of the lake-trail junction (~1,500 ft gain), bushwhacks ENE through ~500 ft of steep brush to treeline, then ~1,000 ft of scree SSE to the SW ridge; it merges into the South Ridge near 9,600 ft and both continue to Red Saddle and the pinnacle. Mountain Project lists them as separate route pages, and our logged tracks differ (686897 Shale Lake South Ridge vs 3274250/2993630 SW ridge). No Southwest row is stored.
recommendation: ADD a Southwest Ridge row on or_mt_jefferson; keep South Ridge unchanged. Optionally raise South Ridge grade from 4th toward Easy 5th (pinnacle class 4 to 5.4 per Mountain Project).

proposed.name: Southwest Ridge
proposed.overview: The usual one-day line to the summit pinnacle, long and tedious rather than technical. A steep brushy bushwhack leads to a loose scree ridge that merges with the South Ridge high on the mountain, then to Red Saddle, a 250 ft steep snow traverse, and the pinnacle, which is class 4 to low 5th depending on the line. Expect loose rock and rockfall on the traverse.
proposed.approach: From Pamelia Lake Trailhead take the lake trail to the Pacific Crest Trail and go south about 20 minutes. Leave the trail near 1,500 ft of gain and push through steep brush east-northeast to treeline, then climb scree to the ridge. There is no reliable water on the ridge; a permit is required at Pamelia Lake for day or overnight use.
proposed.descent_text: Reverse to Red Saddle, then scree-ski the face between the southwest and south ridges and traverse back to the southwest ridge near 8,000 ft. Rappelling the pinnacle is possible, but downclimbing loose fourth class is the alternative.
